units.name: Terror Drone

tier.basis: Built at the War Factory with no further tech; the wiki lists it as tier 1.

cost_band.basis: A little over half the price of a main battle tank.

mobility.notes: One of the fastest ground units in the game. It crosses water and can even reach submerged submarines. Its handling is strafe rather than the pivot default for many legs, because it is a small unit on legs (handling tie-break, reason 1).

body.notes: A spider-like robot that the sources call small or diminutive. Although it comes from the vehicle factory, the game handles it like infantry: it fills an infantry seat in troop transports, so it is coded small. It heals only at a captured hospital or dry dock or at top veterancy, not from an engineer's medical tent or from repair drones.

armour.notes: Very little health. Machine guns and snipers hurt it badly and electric weapons do many times normal damage; melee animals and radiation can't hurt it. Step 4 of the armour-class order decided: its armour set has no plain armour word, and drones are light.

sensors.notes: The wiki gives one sight figure, half the Conscript's vision figure that the registry compares single figures with, so short. Patch 1.11 lengthened its view in stasis ray mode.

armament.name: Dismantler Claws
armament.summary: Closes to touching distance and strikes. Infantry die in one strike. A vehicle or ship (even a submerged one) gets the drone inside it and takes damage from within until it dies or the drone is removed. Aircraft can be infested only while landed. If its own damage destroys the host, the drone can escape (it parachutes down from an aircraft) and attack again. If anything else destroys the host first, the drone dies with it.

armament.name: Electro-Stasis Ray
armament.condition: In stasis mode, switched with the mode toggle.
armament.summary: A long-range beam that pins a vehicle in place: it can't move, transform or deploy, but its guns still work. One documented exception, the Allied aircraft carrier, is shut down completely.

crew.notes: One player is the drone. While it is inside a host, the camera rides along with the host.

abilities.name: Electro-Stasis Ray / Dismantler Claws
abilities.summary: Swaps between the claws and the stasis ray. It uses one at a time, so pinning and infesting the same target takes two drones.

strengths.why: One of the fastest ground units, so it scouts well and reaches vehicles quickly.
Can't be shot normally once inside a vehicle; the enemy must repair or teleport the host, use one of a few special attacks, or lose it.
Kills infantry in one strike, even elite commandos who aren't shooting at it.
Crosses water and reaches even submerged submarines.
The stasis ray outranges most guns.
Cheap and quick to build, so losing one costs little.

weaknesses.why: Very little health: machine guns, snipers and electric weapons destroy it quickly.
The claws need touching distance, so it is exposed on the approach and can't reach aircraft.
One mode at a time, and the ray stops movement but not the target's guns.
Dies with the host if someone else destroys the vehicle first.
Electric weapons do many times normal damage, and normal repair can't heal it.

countered_by.why: Neither weapon can hit aircraft in the air; it survives only by staying away from them or hiding inside an enemy vehicle or a friendly Bullfrog transport.
Machine-gun and autocannon fire does extra damage to it, so anti-infantry escorts shred approaching drones.
Electric weapons do many times normal damage to it.
Repair drones, Multigunners carrying an engineer, and repair stations such as the Crusher Crane, Mecha Bay or War Factory strip an infesting drone out of the host.
Snipers pick it off from range, and some can clear an infested vehicle.

counters.why: Vehicles, especially unarmed ones such as ore collectors and construction vehicles, die to an infesting drone unless they reach repairs or other help in time.
Kills infantry in one strike if they don't shoot it first.
Infestation and the stasis ray stop a unit transforming or deploying, trapping it in its current form.

combos.why: A second drone, or any teammate with a pin, holds the vehicle still so this one can jump in.
A Twinblade helicopter or Bullfrog transport carries several drones at once, giving them extra mobility.
Drones hold enemy vehicles in place while heavier teammates destroy them.

units.memorable: A small, disposable robot that hides inside the enemy's own tank: once it's in, ordinary fire can't reach it, so the enemy has to cure the host.
units.as_player: A cheap, very fast and fragile T1 pick: drawn small and low, with a soldier-sized hitbox outlined in team colour so it can be hit from above. Dive a vehicle to ride inside and chew it up, or hang back and pin it for your team. Aircraft, machine guns and electric weapons are its nightmare.

uncertain.note: No source gives the stasis ray's exact range or duration; a patch note implies the drone keeps the beam on the target rather than firing once.

No source gives the ray's reach. It is long by the profile's words (it outranges most other weapons). The drone's single sight figure is shorter than any long reach would be, but a reach known only from words counts as passing the sight only when a source says so, and none does, so the ray stays long rather than off-screen. Patch 1.11 lengthened the drone's view in stasis ray mode.

The official profile says only repair crews at facilities can remove an infesting drone; the main wiki lists many more ways (repair drones, teleporting the host, several special attacks). The entry follows the wiki.

Game data gives the claws explosive-type damage against vehicles and a sniper-type hit against infantry big enough to kill even a commando at once; 'melee' is used only because the blades family requires it.
Sources call it small or diminutive and no source compares it with a soldier; it is coded small because it fills a soldier's seat in transports.
The infobox's sight figure has no label, while the Hammer tank's page splits vision from fog clearing, so it isn't clear which one this is, or whether it predates patch 1.11.

fit_notes.note: Game data gives the claws explosive-type damage against vehicles and sniper-type damage against infantry, which maps to kinetic. The blades family allows only melee, electric or energy damage, so a player version may want explosive or kinetic.
The beam only immobilises: the target can't move, transform or deploy, but its weapons keep working (the Allied aircraft carrier is the one exception). The emp damage type stands for a full shutdown.

units.name: Hammer Tank

tier.basis: The Hammer tank page's infobox lists it as tier 2; it needs a Super Reactor.

cost_band.basis: The Hammer tank page's price falls in our medium band for RA3; with the Mass Production upgrade it drops to the low band.

mobility.notes: Slower than the Allied main battle tank and not amphibious. Heavy enough to run over infantry, but crushing is a fallback, not a plan.

armour.notes: The toughest of the three factions' main battle tanks. Machine-gun fire does much less damage to it. Facing matters only mildly: side and rear hits do slightly more (game data on the wiki). Step 3 of the armour-class order decided: its armour set name is not a plain armour word, and the game's cost anchor averages its price with the other two main battle tanks, so heavy.

sensors.notes: The wiki gives a vision figure and a fog-clearing figure more than twice as large. As the registry says, the fog-clearing figure counts; it equals the Conscript's, so medium. Patch 1.11 lengthened its view in leech mode.

armament.name: 85 mm cannon
armament.summary: A fast-firing anti-vehicle gun. Poor against infantry and unable to hit aircraft.

armament.name: Leech Beam
armament.condition: In leech mode. Since patch 1.11 the tank must stand still to use it.
armament.summary: Reaches about twice as far as the cannon. Deals modest damage that ignores armour type, and repairs the tank while it stays on target. A vehicle that dies in the beam can hand over its weapon if the tank has none yet.

armament.name: Auxiliary weapon port
armament.condition: Filled once, by a vehicle that dies in the leech beam; can't be swapped. It is kept for the life of the tank, except that losing a Sky Knight drone taken from an aircraft carrier frees the slot in the base game (not in Uprising).
armament.summary: Empty when built. Holds one weapon taken from the dead vehicle, such as anti-air flak, an anti-infantry gun, a tesla coil or artillery. It fires alongside the cannon, one weapon at a time, and is silent in leech mode; a Sky Knight drone taken from an aircraft carrier is the one exception; a Multigunner IFV gives anti-air rockets whoever rides inside.

crew.notes: One player drives, fires the cannon and holds the beam. A two-seat version could give the beam and the stolen weapon to a second player.

abilities.name: Leech Beam (mode switch)
abilities.summary: Switches between the cannon and the leech beam. Leeching kills more slowly than the cannon; it is a choice to heal or to loot, not to deal more damage.

abilities.name: Weapon salvage
abilities.summary: When a vehicle dies while held in the beam, whoever lands the kill, a tank with an empty port mounts that vehicle's weapon and can't swap it later. It works on friendly vehicles with force-fire. Structures give nothing, and neither do a few vehicles, among them the Grinder, the Mortar Cycle and some ships and submarines.

on_death.notes: A Soviet protocol the player can pick can make destroyed Soviet vehicles release a Terror Drone; that is a faction power, not this unit's own outcome.

strengths.why: Its armour is rated the heaviest among main battle tanks, which makes it the toughest of the three; beats the Allied and Imperial tanks one-on-one.
Heals itself mid-fight with the beam, so a damaged tank can step behind the line and leech at range to recover instead of leaving the battle.
A stolen weapon can cover its own gaps, such as anti-air or anti-infantry, or add a big-unit gun.
The beam outranges basic defences such as small turrets.
Runs over infantry caught in the open.

weaknesses.why: Its cannon can't hit aircraft and is poor against infantry; without a stolen weapon it has no answer to air.
While leeching it stands still, kills slowly and its stolen weapon goes quiet (a stolen Sky Knight drone is the one exception). The player version slows it heavily instead of rooting it.
A stolen weapon can't be swapped, so a poor first steal can't be undone.
Needs a Super Reactor built first.
Slower than the Allied tank and can't cross water.

countered_by.why: Bombers and gunships hit it freely when it has no stolen anti-air weapon.
The official notes call anti-tank infantry a real threat, since its cannon is poor against small targets.
Infesting drones ride inside it, where its weapons can't reach them, or pin it with a ray.
The beam can't target the drone. As the drone's own entry describes, it can ride inside the tank, where it can't be shot, or pin the tank in place with its ray.

counters.why: Beats the other factions' main battle tanks one-on-one thanks to heavier armour and steady damage.
The beam outranges basic defences such as small turrets.

combos.why: The official notes pair it with an anti-infantry walker to cover its blind spot.
An anti-air escort, or leeching a friendly anti-air vehicle on purpose, covers its weakness to aircraft.
Teammates soften a big enemy vehicle while the tank holds the beam on it; the tank still gets the weapon if someone else lands the kill.

units.memorable: A main battle tank that loots: the first weapon it takes from a vehicle dying in its beam is its one-time loadout choice, since it holds only one stolen gun and can't swap it.
units.as_player: A mid-tier brawler with a cannon on left mouse. The turret turns slowly, so a close flanker can get round it. Hold Q for a long tether that heals you while it holds; while tethering you are heavily slowed but not rooted, your turret stays locked on the target and the cannon is silent. Tether what your team is already killing: if it dies in your beam, a tier-scaled copy of its gun goes on right mouse for this life.

units.name: Multigunner IFV

tier.basis: Built at the Allied Armor Facility with no further tech; the wiki lists it as tier 1.

cost_band.basis: The wiki's price from patch 1.08 on falls in our low band for RA3; before that patch it sat in the medium band, and an early beta priced it lower still.

mobility.notes: Outruns most ground vehicles. Not amphibious, and it can't crush infantry.

body.notes: No rotating turret: in the game the whole car turns to aim (its Red Alert 2 ancestor had a turret). The wiki calls it an up-armoured dune buggy, the official profile an armoured car; its size is inferred from that, as no source gives dimensions. Most passenger types show their own roof weapon model (the wiki's gallery shows each version). The player version adds a free-aiming roof turret for the passenger only (see crew notes).

armour.notes: Light armour (the wiki calls it very light); it trades armour for speed. Step 2 of the armour-class order decided: the wiki's infobox gives the armour word Light.

sensors.notes: No cited page gives a vision range, so the sight is the medium proposal. The source gives it no radar; a player version could add a warning against aircraft.

armament.name: Multipurpose missile launcher
armament.condition: Only when nobody is riding inside.
armament.summary: Rapid, light missiles. Against aircraft they hit about three times as hard, and reach about twice as far, as against ground targets. Good against aircraft and light vehicles, weak against armour.

armament.name: Repair tool (any engineer)
armament.condition: An engineer of any faction rides inside.
armament.summary: Replaces the weapon with a repair tool for friendly vehicles. It drives to nearby damaged friends on its own and removes Terror Drones from them. It can't attack.

armament.name: Stun bark (attack dog)
armament.condition: An Allied attack dog rides inside.
armament.summary: Loudspeakers amplify the dog's bark to stun enemy infantry for a few seconds at long range. Commandos are immune.

armament.name: Stun roar (war bear)
armament.condition: A Soviet war bear rides inside.
armament.summary: Loudspeakers amplify the bear's roar to stun enemy infantry for a few seconds at long range, over a slightly larger area than the dog version. Commandos are immune.

armament.name: Auto-shotgun (Peacekeeper)
armament.condition: An Allied Peacekeeper rides inside.
armament.summary: A close-range shotgun that knocks infantry back.

armament.name: Missile pod (Javelin soldier)
armament.condition: An Allied Javelin soldier rides inside.
armament.summary: Fires a large burst of rockets, then pauses a few seconds to reload. Lets the car take on heavier units, though the wiki says it does only half damage to tanks, King Onis, ore collectors and Assault Destroyers.

armament.name: Sniper rifle (Spy)
armament.condition: An Allied Spy rides inside.
armament.summary: Kills infantry in one shot and can fire on the move. Also hits terror drones, but no vehicles.

armament.name: Anti-infantry autocannons (Tanya)
armament.condition: Tanya, the Allied commando, rides inside.
armament.summary: The commando's own guns, mounted with identical stats: shreds groups of infantry but can attack nothing else.

armament.name: Cryo beam (Cryo Legionnaire)
armament.condition: An Allied Cryo Legionnaire rides inside (Uprising only).
armament.summary: A single freezing beam that can also freeze aircraft, which then fall and shatter. It reaches further than the Cryo Legionnaire on foot or the Cryocopter.

armament.name: Gatling gun (Conscript)
armament.condition: A Soviet Conscript rides inside.
armament.summary: A weak gatling gun; even against infantry it is not very effective.

armament.name: Flak cannon (Flak Trooper)
armament.condition: A Soviet Flak Trooper rides inside.
armament.summary: Anti-air only, a little stronger than the Soviets' own flak transport, on a fast chassis that keeps up with aircraft.

armament.name: Tesla gun (Tesla Trooper)
armament.condition: A Soviet Tesla Trooper rides inside.
armament.summary: Kills infantry in one zap and hurts vehicles and buildings. A beta patch added a pre-attack delay and lowered its overall damage output.

armament.name: Radiation spray (Desolator)
armament.condition: A Soviet Desolator rides inside (Uprising only).
armament.summary: The Desolator's own radiation spray with identical stats, good for clearing groups of infantry.

armament.name: Piercing sniper rifle (Natasha)
armament.condition: Natasha, the Soviet commando, rides inside.
armament.summary: Kills several infantry in a line, but can't fire while moving.

armament.name: Infantry laser (Imperial Warrior)
armament.condition: An Empire Imperial Warrior rides inside.
armament.summary: An anti-infantry laser that is also fair against light vehicles.

armament.name: Anti-vehicle laser (Tankbuster)
armament.condition: An Empire Tankbuster rides inside.
armament.summary: A fast-firing anti-vehicle laser with a much longer reach than the soldier on foot; StrategyWiki rates the combination as highly versatile and strong.

armament.name: Shuriken launcher (Shinobi)
armament.condition: An Empire Shinobi rides inside.
armament.summary: Throws shuriken that deal heavy sniper-type damage to infantry, firing slightly faster than the Spy version.

armament.name: Bow launcher (Archer Maiden)
armament.condition: An Empire Archer Maiden rides inside (Uprising only).
armament.summary: Arrows that hit both aircraft and infantry, with a little more anti-air reach than on foot.

armament.name: Psychokinetic blast (Yuriko Omega)
armament.condition: Yuriko Omega, the Empire's psychic commando, rides inside.
armament.summary: A mounted version of her psychic attack. The gain is mostly range, speed and protection rather than damage.

crew.notes: One driver and one infantry passenger; the single passenger seat is in-game. Proposal for a player version: the passenger's class sets the roof weapon, and the passenger fires it from a small roof turret that aims freely while the driver steers (the official profile already describes a 'multiturret', though in the game it has no turret and the whole car turns to fire). The driver's own missiles stay fixed forward and are aimed by turning the car.

abilities.name: Weapon changes with the passenger
abilities.summary: Loading one infantry swaps the missiles for a vehicle-mounted version of that soldier's weapon or role: some stronger than on foot, some identical. Unloading brings the missiles back.

on_death.notes: In the source the rider dies with the car; the player version throws both players out hurt, as bail-out says.

strengths.why: Outruns most ground vehicles: a cheap anti-air escort and rapid responder from the first minutes.
Empty, its missiles reach every aircraft, jets and airships included, hitting them about three times as hard as ground targets from about twice as far.
The same missiles, with the same extra damage and reach, work against helicopters and other low fliers.
Changes role mid-match by swapping the passenger: anti-air, anti-tank, anti-infantry, stun or field repair.
With an engineer aboard it repairs tanks in the field and pulls infesting drones out of them.

weaknesses.why: Light armour; it trades armour for speed.
Empty, its missiles deal only light damage to armour, partly offset by their high rate of fire.

A passenger without an anti-air weapon removes its anti-air ability, and in RA3 the passenger dies with the car: one kill for the price of two. The player version throws both players out hurt instead.
Can't cross water or crush infantry, and with no turret the whole car must turn to fire; the player version keeps this only for the driver's own missiles.

countered_by.why: Tanks shrug off its light missiles unless an anti-armour passenger rides along.
Carrying a passenger without an anti-air weapon replaces its missiles, so it can no longer fire back at aircraft.
A Hammer tank shrugs off its light missiles, and leeching the car to death gives the Hammer an anti-air rocket weapon, whoever was riding inside.
An infesting drone kills it from inside unless another Multigunner carrying an engineer, repair drones or a repair station removes it.
An infesting Terror Drone kills it unless repair drones, an engineer-loaded Multigunner, a Chronosphere teleport or a few special attacks remove it (see the Terror Drone's entry).

counters.why: Its default missiles are built for anti-air, with extra damage and range against aircraft.
With a sniper, commando, tesla or radiation passenger it deletes infantry while staying hard to catch.
With an engineer aboard it strips infesting drones out of friendly vehicles; with a spy it can shoot drones.

combos.why: Engineer cars repair the main tanks in the field.
Ferries engineers quickly across the battlefield for sabotage runs.
Most infantry types are a loadout: the team's infantry mix decides what the cars can do.

units.memorable: A cheap, fast car whose gun is whoever sits in it: the soldier you load decides whether it hunts aircraft, snipes infantry, kills tanks or repairs them.
units.as_player: A two-seat T1 runabout. Alone, the driver fires rapid light missiles, best against aircraft, on left mouse and aims them by turning the car. A teammate who climbs in (E) gets a small roof turret with a mounted version of their class weapon and aims it freely while you drive; your missiles stay silent until they leave or you evict them (G). If the car dies, both players are thrown out hurt.

The Hammer tank and Terror Drone entries under 'Countered by', and the repair drones and repair stations in the infesting-drone entry, rest on those units' own cited pages (the Hammer tank page and the Terror drone page); none of this unit's three sources covers them.

units.name: Mecha Tengu

tier.basis: Built at the Mecha Bay with no further tech: its infobox gives tier 1, and the Mecha bay page lists it with the basic units.

cost_band.basis: Its price is a little under the registry's medium threshold, about four fifths of a main battle tank's, so low.

mobility.notes: The infobox land speed is twice the Conscript's; over water it is somewhat slower, and hover units are banded by land speed. That is about a third faster than the Hammer tank, the Soviet main battle tank, and the profile says it outruns most vehicles. It floats a few metres up on its boosters and skims over ground that would slow infantry or simpler vehicles, so it crosses water on its own (the infobox marks it amphibious). Two beta patches raised its speeds and then put them back. In jet form it is much faster (see modes). Drift is the hover default.

body.notes: An anthropomorphic robot whose arms and legs act as stabilizers rather than for walking; the wiki calls it a hover walker and the profile a dual-form combat robot. Humanoid mech is the shape; it breaks that body's class and mobility rules (see atypical). Medium as a light mech; no source gives its dimensions. In jet form it folds into a fighter airframe (see modes).

armour.notes: Step 4 of the armour-class order decided: RA3 has no armour map, its armour set's name is not a plain armour word, and a light walker bigger than a soldier is medium. Its alloy shrugs off small arms: rifle-type gun damage does a quarter of normal since patch 1.11 (half before that, and still half in Uprising), and sniper and melee hits do nothing; cannon, prism and tesla hits do well over normal. Directional by the Uprising manual's armour-facing rule for armoured vehicles; its page gives no side or rear figures. The profile says current models are lighter and less sturdy than older ones. The jet form uses an aircraft armour set (see modes).

sensors.notes: The infobox gives a shroud-clearing figure equal to the Conscript's, so medium. Its vision figure in hover form also equals the Conscript's; the jet's vision is a little longer since patch 1.11.

armament.name: Kinetic burst-shot autocannons (Mecha Tengu)
armament.summary: Twin autocannons, one each side of the air intake, fire quick accurate bursts; the manual calls the gun a 20mm autocannon. They shred soldiers and light vehicles, yet tanks shrug them off. In this form the unit attacks only targets on the ground or on the water, never aircraft; that includes buildings such as refineries on the water. The profile says it has to steady itself before it fires.

armament.name: Kinetic burst-shot autocannons (Jet Tengu)
armament.condition: In jet form, after transforming.
armament.summary: The same guns once the unit is a jet: they now hit only aircraft, reach a little further and hit much harder than in hover form. They do only a quarter of their damage to Apollo fighters, MiG fighters and other Jet Tengus, and double damage to the Harbinger gunship. Patch 1.05 raised their damage and patch 1.11 made Jet Tengus much weaker against each other. There is no ammunition to reload at an airfield.

crew.notes: The background text gives it a pilot in a full-body cockpit; as an RTS unit it has no player seats, so solo is our proposal. One player flies both forms.

abilities.name: Mecha Mode / Jet Mode
abilities.summary: Switches between the hover robot and the jet fighter. The change itself takes under a second, but the unit must then wait a medium cooldown before it can switch again, so it should avoid fights while the cooldown runs. Being infested by a Terror Drone, lifted by Yuriko Omega, or hit by a stasis ray or an EMP weapon stops it switching.

modes.name: Jet Tengu
modes.summary: Folds into a conventional fighter shape and flies high, at about twice its hover speed and four times the Conscript's (a little slower than the Apollo and MiG fighters). Its guns switch to the jet weapon, which can hit only aircraft, so only anti-air weapons reach it and it cannot hurt ground targets. Its armour becomes an aircraft set that takes normal damage from autocannon, flak and rocket fire (light, as planes are). The profile says its wings let it hover in place while it attacks, which forward-only handling does not show. It is the Empire's main air-superiority fighter and needs no airfield. If destroyed in this form it crashes and hurts what is near.

on_death.notes: Only in jet form: the crashing jet deals explosive damage in a small area (infobox notes). Destroyed in hover form, it is simply gone. Honorable Discharge, an Imperial protocol bought for the whole side, makes destroyed Imperial vehicles explode and makes this crash about three times as strong; that is a side-wide power, not the unit's own outcome.

strengths.why: Its burst-fire autocannons cut through soldiers and light vehicles, and its alloy shrugs off their rifles.
Changes form in under a second: it can flee a losing ground fight into the air, or drop down on ground units that were chasing a fighter.
As a jet it is the Empire's early air-superiority fighter, with no ammunition limit and no airfield to return to, so numbers can swarm enemy fighters.
Outruns most vehicles on the ground, and the jet form is faster still, which suits early raids on refineries and derricks.
Moves and fights over water nearly as well as on land, so it can harass refineries out at sea.

weaknesses.why: Each form hits only its own layer: the robot cannot shoot aircraft, and the jet cannot shoot ground targets, so ground anti-air kills it freely. After a switch it must wait out a cooldown, and infestation, psychic lifting, stasis rays and EMP stop it switching, so it can be caught in the wrong form.
In hover form its guns are no match for tanks, and in jet form they do only a quarter of their damage to Apollo and MiG fighters, so it loses to them one on one.

countered_by.why: Tanks shrug off its autocannons, and their cannons do well over normal damage to it, so they destroy it easily.
In jet form it cannot fire at the ground, so ground anti-air shoots it down freely, and dedicated fighters beat it one on one.
Its jet guns do only a quarter of their damage to the Apollo, so a lone Jet Tengu loses; only numbers win.
Its jet guns do only a quarter of their damage to the MiG, so a lone Jet Tengu loses; only numbers win.
Its missiles hit both ground and air targets, so it threatens the Tengu in either form.

counters.why: Shreds soldiers with its autocannons while their rifles barely scratch its alloy.
Light vehicles fall to its autocannons too, so it can stand up to most early units.
As a jet it hunts aircraft that cannot shoot back at other aircraft, and Harbinger gunships take double damage from it.

combos.why: Works best in numbers: flocks of Jet Tengus overwhelm better enemy fighters, and groups raid economies.
Tags along with tank hunters such as Tankbusters, which cannot shoot aircraft and do poorly against infantry, covering both gaps by switching form.

units.memorable: A hover mech that folds into a jet fighter in an instant: one moment it shreds infantry, the next it is hunting aircraft, but each form can only hit its own layer.
units.as_player: A quick T1 hover mech. Left mouse fires twin nose autocannons, aimed by turning, that tear up infantry and light vehicles but lose to tanks and cannot touch aircraft. Press Q to snap into a jet: much faster, up where only anti-air reaches you, guns now hitting only aircraft. The switch is instant but locks for a medium cooldown, so the wrong form can get you killed. Go down as a jet and your crash hurts whatever is below.

uncertain.note: The one designation for both forms names two roles. Step 1 takes anti-infantry because the main weapon, the hover form's guns, has the bonus: the profile says they cut through infantry, and basic infantry armour (Conscript (Red Alert 3) page, Command & Conquer Wiki) takes half again normal Auto Cannon damage. The anti-air bonus belongs to the jet's alternate weapon, not to the main weapon.

Anti-air ranks at step 1 (the designation). Raider is supported only at step 2, through the transform mode: the very fast, light jet form is how it hits and then escapes (the wiki says it can flee a losing fight by transforming and that it excels at early harassment). Step 4 cannot give raider, since the hover form's armour is medium. If a mode's speed and armour do not count for raider, the second slot would be assault (step 4: medium armour and a medium-range main weapon), although the sources describe a harasser rather than a unit that leads pushes.

Medium by step 4 as a light walker bigger than a soldier. Light is arguable: as a hovercraft its kind is named in no class description; its health is close to that of the light Multigunner IFV (Multigunner IFV page); and StrategyWiki calls its armour poor. But small arms hurt it less than they hurt the Hammer tank (Hammer tank page), and the Riptide ACV, an APC and so medium by kind, uses the same armour set (Riptide ACV page, Command & Conquer Wiki).

Directional only by the Uprising manual's rule for armoured vehicles: the Mecha Tengu page gives no side or rear figures, and the manual makes the rear sound much weaker than any infobox figure in the game does.

The infobox names one weapon for both forms, with separate ground and air attack lines and a range for each form, and the profile calls them the very same guns. The form decides what they can hit, so the jet version is coded as an alternate weapon with the jet mode (Paired entries) rather than one entry for both.

The Mecha Tengu page says the jet guns do a quarter of their damage to Apollo fighters, while the Apollo fighter page (Command & Conquer Wiki) says the Apollo takes a little under a third of normal damage from Jet Tengus. Either way a lone Jet Tengu loses to an Apollo.

Structures rest on the wiki's remark that it can pester refineries on the water and on the profile's account of Tengus wrecking a super-reactor; no infobox line names buildings. The Mecha Mode button text names ground and water targets only.
Only the 2008 profile says it must steady itself to fire; no other source read confirms whether it can fire on the move.

Jet, from its name, its fighter shape, its high flight and its role as a fighter. Hovering flight is arguable: the wiki calls it a VTOL fighter, the profile says its wings let it hover in place to attack, and the hovering-flight term names VTOL. The Apollo fighter and MiG fighter pages (Command & Conquer Wiki) describe the other sides' fighters as VTOL too, and give their air speeds, which the mode summary compares.
Forward-only is the jet default and the handling tie-break gives no reason to change it in a commanded game, although the profile says the jet can hover in place while it attacks.
Size is left at the base form's medium. The sizes list names jets as large, but the same unit only folds into its other shape.
The comparison with the Hammer tank uses that tank's land speed from the Hammer tank page (Command & Conquer Wiki).
The infobox's crash damage is over a small radius; the registry note for ra3 counts it as a death blast. It applies only when the unit dies as a jet.

fit_notes.wanted: a fixed-wing flight type that can also hover in place (a VTOL fighter)
fit_notes.note: Jet means it must keep moving and attacks in passes; hovering flight means a rotor or VTOL craft flying low. Red Alert 3's fighters, the Jet Tengu among them, are VTOL jets that fly high and still hover to attack.

fit_notes.wanted: a trait for a weapon the unit must stop to fire
fit_notes.note: The profile says the hover form has to steady itself before it fires; no weapon trait says the unit cannot fire while moving.

atypical.note: Its shape is a humanoid robot with arms and legs, but they only steady it while it hovers; the class follows how it moves (an air cushion over land and water), and our humanoid mech body is listed for walkers only.
The humanoid mech body is listed only for two legs, but this robot never walks: it hovers a few metres up on its boosters.

units.name: Sudden Transport

tier.basis: Built at the Mecha Bay with no further tech: its infobox gives tier 1, and the Mecha bay page lists it with the basic units.

cost_band.basis: Its price sits exactly on the registry's low threshold, about half a main battle tank's, and a price on an edge takes the higher band, so low.

mobility.notes: The infobox gives one speed for both land and water, twice the Conscript's. That is about a third faster than the Hammer tank, the Soviet main battle tank. As a hovercraft it crosses water by itself (the infobox and the manual call it amphibious). Drift is the hover default.

body.notes: An enclosed hover hull with its riders hidden inside; the wiki calls it a hover armoured personnel carrier. It carries no weapon or turret. Medium as an APC; no source gives its dimensions.

armour.notes: Step 4 of the armour-class order decided: RA3 has no armour map, its armour set's name is not a plain armour word (the registry note says set names never are), and an APC is medium. Melee and sniper hits do nothing to it, gun and autocannon fire does half damage, radiation almost nothing; flak, rocket, cannon, prism and tesla fire does half again normal damage. Its infobox gives slightly more damage from the side and a little more again from the rear, so directional, though the difference is small.

sensors.notes: The infobox gives a shroud-reveal figure equal to the Conscript's shroud-clearing figure, so medium. Its disguise is an ability (disguise pattern), not the stealth trait: it stays in view and only looks like another vehicle.

crew.notes: Five infantry seats, copied from the source; no page shows riders firing out, so they are cargo. No crew is named in the sources; as an RTS unit it has no player seats, so solo is our proposal: the buyer drives.

abilities.name: Passenger seats
abilities.summary: Carries up to five infantry over land and water; they cannot act until they get out. Letting them out (its Evacuate button, our evict key) ends the disguise.

abilities.name: Disguise
abilities.summary: Targeting a vehicle of either side makes the transport take on that vehicle's look; the manual adds other objects, and the wiki notes that in a match against the AI, with no vehicle at hand to copy, it can even look like an aircraft at ground level. Most base defences and units are fooled. Detector units (the Allied attack dog, the Soviet war bear and the Imperial Burst Drone) see through it, and alert players can too, because it keeps its own speed rather than its model's and may copy a vehicle that cannot go on water. The disguise ends when the riders get out.

on_death.notes: The infobox gives explosive damage when it is destroyed, and StrategyWiki says the explosion kills what is close by and the infantry still inside. Honorable Discharge, an Imperial protocol bought for the whole side, makes every destroyed Imperial vehicle explode; that is a side-wide power, not this unit's own outcome.

strengths.why: Passes as any vehicle, so most base defences and units let it through and its riders can unload in the middle of an enemy base.
Five seats are enough for an ambush party of Imperial Warriors, Tankbusters or Shinobi, or a team of engineers.
Crosses land and water at the same speed, so it can come in from the sea.
Outpaces main battle tanks, so it puts troops in place quickly.
Cheap and available from the start, so a few of them dressed as stronger vehicles make a convincing decoy group.

weaknesses.why: Not foolproof: detector animals and drones see through it, and watchful players notice a speed that does not match its model or a land vehicle out on the water.
Letting the riders out ends the disguise, which usually gets it destroyed, and when it dies the riders still inside die with it.

countered_by.why: Detectors see through its disguise, and once it is found the unarmed transport cannot fight back.
Allied attack dogs see through the disguise.
Soviet war bears see through the disguise.
Burst Drones, the Empire's own flying scouts, see through the disguise.
Cannon and rocket fire does half again normal damage to it, and it has no weapon to answer with once it is found.

counters.why: Most base defences cannot see through the disguise, so it slips past them and drops troops inside the base.

combos.why: A load of engineers can sneak deep into a base and capture key buildings such as the construction yard.
Imperial Warriors, Tankbusters or Shinobi spilling out inside a base wreak havoc and distract the enemy from an attack elsewhere.
Dressed as stronger vehicles, cheap transports pad out an armoured group and draw the enemy's eye away from the real attack force.

units.memorable: A cheap hover carrier that takes the look of any vehicle it points at, so five soldiers can drive into an enemy base dressed as one of its own tanks.
units.as_player: An unarmed T1 hover carrier with five seats for teammates. Point at any vehicle (Q) to look like it to the enemy, then slip past defences and drop your riders (G) where they hurt most; unloading ends the disguise. Detector scouts see through it, and so does a speed that does not match your disguise or a land tank driving on water. If you die you blow up, taking your riders and anything close with you.

The wiki's ability box lists Evacuate, which drops the disguise and unloads everyone at once. It is left off as the evict key (registry note for ra3); the disguise ends whenever riders get out anyway.

Medium by step 4 as an APC. Its armour set's name contains the word Light, but the registry note treats set names as no armour word, and its health is only a little above that of the light Multigunner IFV (Multigunner IFV page, Command & Conquer Wiki).

Infiltrator rests on step 2: the disguise, a button every copy has, lets it pass as an enemy vehicle, which the role's description and tie-break name. No official text calls it an infiltrator or a spy.
Only StrategyWiki says the riders die with it; the Command & Conquer Wiki page says nothing about riders when it is destroyed. No page gives the blast's radius.
The comparison with the Hammer tank uses that tank's land speed from the Hammer tank page (Command & Conquer Wiki).

The Burst Drone, War bear (Red Alert 3) and Attack dog (Red Alert 3) pages on the Command & Conquer Wiki agree with the Stealth page that these units find disguised enemies; the Burst Drone page names Sudden Transports outright.

units.name: Sickle

tier.basis: The Sickle page's infobox gives tier 1: the War Factory builds it with no further tech.

cost_band.basis: The Sickle page's price sits exactly on the lowest price of our medium band for RA3, so it takes that band; it is a little cheaper than a main battle tank.

mobility.notes: Twice the Conscript's ground speed by the wiki's game values, and about a third faster than the Hammer, the Soviet main battle tank; the wiki ranks its speed near the top of the game's vehicles. It cannot cross water. Walking, it runs over nothing: its own crush level is nil, and only a Flea Jump landing lifts it above the level at which infantry are crushed (see abilities). Handling stays pivot, the default for many legs, since it is neither tiny nor small and no source shows a reason to change it.

body.notes: A compact pod held up on tall stilt legs, with its three guns in separate ball-shaped canopies around the pod rather than in one turret. The official profile calls the shape spiderlike and gives it four legs. StrategyWiki calls it a light walker, which our Sizes examples put at medium; no source gives its dimensions.

armour.notes: Step 4 of the armour-class order decided: its armour set's name is not a plain armour word, and our class descriptions put a light walker bigger than a soldier at medium. Its health is a little below the Hammer tank's. The armour set ignores sniper and melee hits, takes only a quarter of gun damage (half in Uprising) and three quarters of rocket damage, full damage from auto cannon, flak and explosives, and well over full damage from cannon, prism and tesla weapons: it shrugs off small arms but not anti-tank fire. Side hits do slightly more and rear hits a little more again, a small difference.

sensors.notes: The infobox gives a vision figure and a larger shroud-clearing figure. The shroud figure, which the registry says counts, equals the Conscript's, so medium; its vision figure equals the Conscript's too.

armament.name: PKX 12.7 mm heavy machine guns (three)
armament.summary: Three copies of one heavy machine gun, each in its own swivelling ball canopy that turns apart from the hull. Each gun covers a little over a third of the circle, so together they fire all round, keep firing on the move and can work on several targets at once, but at most two of them can aim at any one target. Deadly to infantry and weak against armour; the canopies cannot tilt up far enough to reach aircraft. Its reach equals the Conscript rifle's.

crew.notes: The lore gives each Sickle three gunners, one per gun position, which changes nothing here. One player drives and fires all three guns: they are copies of one gun, so one weapon entry fired on one attack order, and decision 2A hands a gunner only another weapon on its own mount. In a player version the guns whose arcs cover the cursor fire.

abilities.name: Flea Jump
abilities.summary: Leaps to a chosen spot up to about twice its guns' reach away: over walls, roadblocks and other obstacles, and up onto cliffs and plateaus that troops on foot cannot reach. The landing deals melee-category damage in a small circle around it, which the Hammer tank's armour, for one, ignores, so it works on infantry rather than armour. For the jump its crush level rises above the crushable level of ordinary infantry, so it can now and then squash soldiers it lands on; the wiki adds that a well-timed landing can stun commandos. It recharges after a short wait, half of what it was before beta patch 1.5.

on_death.notes: In the source it is simply destroyed; bail-out is the default for a crewed machine. The Terror Drone Surprise protocol, which a player picks for the whole side, can make a destroyed Soviet vehicle release a Terror Drone; that is a faction power, not this unit's own outcome.

strengths.why: Three heavy machine guns cut down infantry, keep firing while it moves and can work on several soldiers at once.
Its three gun arcs together cover every direction, so infantry cannot slip round to an unguarded side.
Flea Jump clears obstacles and reaches plateaus that troops on foot cannot, for scouting or for landing among enemy infantry.
Its speed is near the top of the game's vehicles, so it runs down fleeing infantry and scouts well.
Shrugs off small-arms fire: its armour ignores sniper shots and takes little from guns.

weaknesses.why: No more than two of its three guns can aim at one target, so it does poorly against a single tough target.
Its guns do little to armour and cannot be raised to hit aircraft at all.
Cannon, prism and tesla hits do more than full damage, and even a little anti-tank fire wrecks it.
Its legs cannot carry it across water; the wiki counts the lack of amphibious movement among its flaws.

countered_by.why: Its guns cannot be raised to shoot at fliers, so any armed aircraft can attack it without return fire.
Anti-tank weapons tear through its cheap alloy armour, the official notes say.
Tanks and other heavy weapons do to it what it does to infantry, the wiki says, while its guns barely scratch them.

counters.why: Mows down infantry waves, and a jump into a crowd scatters and crushes them; well timed, it can even stun and kill commandos.

combos.why: The Hammer tank's profile calls the Sickle its natural partner: the tank kills vehicles, the Sickle the infantry its cannon handles poorly.
The Hammer tank's profile calls the Sickle its natural partner: the tank kills vehicles, the Sickle the infantry its cannon handles poorly.
An anti-air escort covers the aircraft its guns cannot reach; the official notes joke about the gap and the Bullfrog sales it brings.
The official notes pair it, tongue in cheek, with the Bullfrog, whose anti-air gun covers the Sickle's blind spot.

units.memorable: A spindly anti-infantry walker whose three swivel guns cover every direction, and which flea-jumps over walls and up cliffs to land among enemy troops.
units.as_player: A fast T1 walker for one player. Three swivel machine guns each cover a wide arc: aim anywhere and the guns facing that way fire, two at most on one target, so you shred infantry all round while moving. Q flea-jumps over walls and up cliffs on a short cooldown; landing in a crowd hurts and can squash soldiers. Tanks, anti-tank fire and anything flying beat you, and water stops you.

The official profile gives the Sickle four stilt legs; no other page read gives a count. Many legs holds whatever the count.

Medium rests on reading it as a light walker, StrategyWiki's word. Its health is a little below the Hammer tank's (Hammer tank page of the Command & Conquer Wiki, https://cnc.fandom.com/wiki/Hammer_tank), but the class descriptions decide by kind, not by health.

The infobox writes the guns' damage category as Auto-Cannon, with a hyphen; it is read as the registry map's Auto Cannon, which gives kinetic. The family stays machine gun, since the sources describe heavy machine guns firing bullets.
No source says how the bullets travel; hitscan is the machine-gun family default.
No source names structures or ships as targets. Structures come from the family's ground kinds (can_target step 4) and ships from the naval rule; the profile rules out aircraft.
That the guns do little to armour rests on StrategyWiki's low-damage verdict and on the Hammer tank page of the Command & Conquer Wiki, whose armour set takes only a quarter of auto cannon damage.
The comparison with the Hammer's speed uses the ground speed on the Hammer tank page of the Command & Conquer Wiki (https://cnc.fandom.com/wiki/Hammer_tank).

Only the main wiki says a well-timed jump stuns commandos; StrategyWiki says the landing knocks infantry down. The wiki's special-ability page (the Command & Conquer Wiki's Special ability (Red Alert 3) page, where Flea Jump redirects) lists Flea Jump as a targeted ability. That the landing spares armour rests on the Hammer tank page of the Command & Conquer Wiki (https://cnc.fandom.com/wiki/Hammer_tank), whose armour set takes no melee damage. No source says whether the landing also hurts friendly units.

fit_notes.wanted: split arcs: several mounts that together cover the whole circle, with only some able to bear on one target
fit_notes.note: Each of the three guns covers a little over a third of the circle, so the set covers every direction while at most two guns reach any one target. Limited arc describes one mount covering part of the circle; no aim term describes overlapping partial arcs.

The manual rates it highly for controlling crowds, and its jump knocks infantry down where it lands (StrategyWiki) or stuns commandos (wiki). Disabler's requires need a stun, root, silence or slow weapon trait, cryo or EMP damage, or a control pattern; a leap that stuns on landing has none of them, so the role is left out.

units.name: Kirov Airship

tier.basis: The Kirov page's infobox gives tier 3: the Airfield builds it, and only while a Battle Lab stands.

cost_band.basis: The Kirov page's price is well above the lowest price of our very-high band for RA3, about two and a half main battle tanks.

mobility.notes: About three fifths of the Conscript's speed by the wiki's air speed figure. Among the game's aircraft it is by far the slowest: about a fifth as fast as the Twinblade and the Century Bomber, and about a seventh as fast as the MiG. The profile and the manual both name slowness as its drawback. Gastroburners nearly double its speed while they burn, which gives it the boost trait; that boosted speed is not its stock speed (see abilities). Handling stays drift, the airship default.

body.notes: A massive rigid dirigible; airships are huge in our Sizes examples.

armour.notes: Step 4 of the armour-class order decided: its armour set's name is not a plain armour word, and our class descriptions name big airships as super-heavy; check A agrees, since it is huge and tier 3. The profile calls it close to indestructible and says most anti-aircraft fire barely troubles it. Its aircraft armour set takes double damage from cannon and gun hits, full damage from auto cannon, flak and rocket hits, three quarters from explosives, and next to nothing from sniper, melee and radiation hits. It mends itself slowly whenever it is not under attack (the infobox), the self-repair model; the faster healing at Heroic rank belongs to veterancy. Gastroburners burn its own health away while they run.

sensors.notes: Its vision figure is shorter than the Conscript's, but its shroud-clearing figure, which the registry says counts, equals the Conscript's, so medium.

armament.name: BOR-57 Grom bombs
armament.summary: Drops heavy bombs on whatever lies directly under it, levelling buildings and slow ground units. Its reach is next to nothing, so it has to fly over each target, and the bombs never reach aircraft. Each blast hurts everything around the impact, friendly units included, though they take only half damage. Unlike the Allied Vindicator and Century Bomber it carries enough bombs for a whole battle and never flies home to rearm.

crew.notes: The lore has decorated officers fly it as pilot-bombardiers who live aboard in comfort, which changes nothing here. One player flies it and drops the bombs.

abilities.name: Gastroburners / Propellers
abilities.summary: Two buttons that undo each other. Gastroburners feed a corrosive chemical into the engines and nearly double the airship's speed, to reach a base sooner, run down slow ground units or get away from anti-air fire, but the chemical eats the hull for as long as it runs, even while the airship hangs in place. Propellers bring back the normal slow speed and stop the damage. Left on too long, the burners bring the airship down.

on_death.notes: The infobox says the falling airship deals heavy explosive damage over an area where it crashes; the profile and StrategyWiki also describe the fall as a big explosion. Burning its Gastroburners too long can bring it down by itself.

strengths.why: Enormous health: the profile says most anti-aircraft fire barely troubles it, so it keeps bombing under fire that would down other aircraft.
Its bombs level buildings quickly; the wiki rates it as lethal to buildings, and the profile says one airship can wreck an entire base.
It never runs out of bombs or flies home to rearm, unlike the Allied bombers.
Mends its hull by itself whenever it is not under attack.
Gastroburners nearly double its speed when it must reach a target or escape anti-air fire.

weaknesses.why: Ponderously slow; the profile names slowness as its one real flaw, so defenders see it coming.
Its only weapon falls straight down, so it has no way at all to fight back against aircraft.
It must fly right over each target, and fast ground units slip out from under it.
Its bombs also hurt friendly units below, at half strength.
Gastroburners eat its own hull and keep doing so even while it hovers; left on, they bring it down.

countered_by.why: Massed anti-air, even light units, can overwhelm it, since its slowness keeps it under fire for a long time.
The wiki names groups of Multigunner IFVs as enough to bring down a Kirov that flies without escorts.
It cannot shoot back at aircraft, and StrategyWiki rates it as easy prey for fighter jets.
Fast ground units dodge its bombs; StrategyWiki says it does poorly against quick ground targets.

counters.why: Deadly against buildings: the profile says even one airship can wreck an entire base.
Slow ground units cannot get out from under its bombs; the wiki rates it as lethal to slow surface units.

combos.why: Escort fighters or anti-air units cover its blind spot; the profile and the wiki both say it should not fly without them.
A ground attack that draws the defenders gives the slow airships time to reach their targets, as the wiki advises.

units.memorable: A colossal, slow airship that never runs out of bombs and can burn its own hull for speed; when it finally falls, the crash is one more bomb.
units.as_player: A T3 flying fortress for one player: huge, very slow and very tough, mending between fights. Drift over targets and drop bombs on whatever is beneath you; teammates under you take half damage. Q toggles Gastroburners: nearly double speed while your own hull burns, until you switch back. You cannot hit anything in the air, so bring anti-air friends, and if you go down, your crash blasts everything below.

units.name: Tanya

tier.basis: Trained at the Boot Camp once the construction yard or Command Hub near it has Max Clearance, and since patch 1.11 only while the player also owns a Defense Bureau (her infobox and changelog). Both gates are t3. The Defense Bureau is recorded because it is the extra building patch 1.11 added and the gate the registry gives other units that need both, such as the FutureTank X-1.

cost_band.basis: Her infobox price, which StrategyWiki repeats, lands exactly on the very-high threshold, so it takes that band: about twice a main battle tank.

mobility.notes: A little quicker than the Conscript on land. Her infobox gives the same figure for swimming, and in water she keeps fighting as well as on foot, so ships and naval bases are within her reach.

armour.notes: The soldier rule decided: her infobox names no armour set, but a beta patch halved what explosive damage does to her, while the Conscript's armour set takes explosives in full, so her game data makes her tougher than the basic rifle infantry and she is light. She has about three times a Conscript's health. One health bar; her real protection is the Time Belt, which undoes recent hits.

sensors.notes: Her shroud-clearing figure equals the Conscript's, so medium; patch 1.11 raised it to that level from a shorter one. Her plain vision figure is well above the Conscript's.

armament.name: Black Buzzard custom pistols (x2)
armament.summary: Two custom pistols fired very fast and very accurately: each shot drops a basic soldier, so she can clear whole groups of infantry on her own. They reach a little less far than the Conscript's rifle and most other infantry rifles. Used only on infantry; her charges handle vehicles, ships and buildings, and nothing she carries can attack aircraft.

armament.name: C4 plastic explosive charges
armament.summary: Her attack order switches to explosives against vehicles, ships and buildings (patch 1.05 gave it its own cursor over vehicles and ships). She runs right up to the target, sets a charge very quickly and the blast destroys it outright, the heaviest tanks included. She carries a large stock and needs no cooldown, so the price is the walk in under fire. Since patch 1.11, Soviet tanks she kills this way no longer release a Terror Drone from the Terror Drone Surprise protocol. It is planted on contact rather than thrown and has no key of its own: the planted variant of throw-explosive.

crew.notes: One player is Tanya. She can ride in a Multigunner IFV, whose gun then becomes a copy of her pistols (see that entry), and, like other infantry, she can garrison buildings, a game-wide mechanic left off here.

abilities.name: Time Belt
abilities.summary: An instant effect on the special-ability key. The FutureTech belt snaps her back to the spot she stood on, with the health she had, several seconds earlier, undoing whatever happened in between. It then needs a short recharge, so it cannot be used back to back. The usual play is to run in, plant charges and rewind out; the Time Belt page adds that she can take a Chronosphere jump into a base and rewind home, and that, unlike a Chronosphere trip, the rewind leaves her free to move at once. How far back it goes differs between sources (see uncertain).

strengths.why: Rapid, accurate pistol fire kills a basic soldier per shot; the official profile credits her with beating whole groups of infantry single-handed.
A planted charge destroys a vehicle, ship or building in one go; official text says not even the strongest Soviet tanks are safe from her charges.
She swims without tiring and fights at sea as well as on land, so ships and harbours are within her reach.

weaknesses.why: Nothing she carries can hit a flier: the pistols are used only on infantry and the charges need contact with a surface target.
Her charges need contact, so she must cross the enemy's fire to reach a vehicle and usually takes heavy damage on the way (StrategyWiki).
Her pistols are outranged by most infantry rifles (StrategyWiki).
One per player, at a very high price, behind Max Clearance and, since patch 1.11, a Defense Bureau as well.

countered_by.why: Neither weapon reaches fliers, so bombers and gunships can hit her freely; StrategyWiki calls her completely ineffective against aircraft.

Infantry freeze almost at once under a cryobeam, and the Cryocopter page names it as a good way to stop a fast commando inside a crowded base; a frozen unit cannot use abilities, so she cannot rewind out.
The same reason in an Allied mirror match: its cryobeam freezes her almost instantly, and any hit then shatters her.

counters.why: Her pistols cut down groups of soldiers; official text says Soviet conscripts cannot stand up to her shooting.
Once she reaches a vehicle, one charge kills it, even an Apocalypse tank.
She swims up to warships and blows them up; official text says no Soviet warship, however big, is safe from her.
Her charges bring down enemy buildings quickly; the Boot Camp's production list sums her up as a commando who detonates buildings.

combos.why: Riding in a Multigunner IFV gives the car a copy of her pistols with the same stats, on a fast armoured chassis.
The same reason: the Multigunner IFV is the car whose gun she sets when she rides inside.

units.memorable: A one-woman strike team who mows down infantry with twin pistols, blows up tanks, ships and buildings with planted charges, and rewinds herself a few seconds, health and all, when a raid goes wrong.
units.as_player: The team's one hero pick at T3: on foot, fragile for her price and deadly up close. Left mouse fires twin pistols that drop a soldier per shot; attack a vehicle, ship or building and walking into it plants a charge that destroys it. Q (Time Belt) snaps you back to where you stood, at the health you had, a few seconds ago: dive, plant, rewind. You swim and fight in water, but nothing you carry touches aircraft.

No damage category is given for the charges, so step 5 decides. Armour-piercing is taken because the sources present the charges as how she kills tanks and ships (official text on battle tanks, the patch 1.05 cursor over vehicles and ships); they are also her tool against buildings, which would argue for the family default, explosive.

No source says how the pistol shots travel; hitscan is the small-arms family default.

Light rests on one changelog line (beta patch 1.5 halved her vulnerability to explosive damage) set against the Conscript's armour set on the Conscript (Red Alert 3) page of the Command & Conquer Wiki, which takes explosives in full. Her own infobox names no armour set, so her other resistances are unknown.

The Boot camp page lists her under tier 3 with Max Clearance only; her own infobox, the Defense bureau page, the Max Clearance page and the patch 1.11 notes on the Command & Conquer Wiki add the Defense Bureau from patch 1.11. Either gate is t3.

Rests on two uncited pages of the Command & Conquer Wiki: the Cryocopter page (cryobeams freeze infantry almost at once and suit a fast commando loose in a base) and the Cryo page (a frozen unit cannot use abilities).

Only anti-armour, from her charges. Infiltrator was considered for the buildings she blows up, but the roles tie-break keeps infiltrator for spying, theft and sabotage from inside, and her charges are set on the target from outside; no other role has both its requires and a sourced part behind it.

fit_notes.note: No registered pattern covers returning yourself to your own earlier position and health on a key. teleport moves you to a spot you choose, and heal-self restores health without undoing your movement; the Time Belt does both at once, but only back to where and how you were a few seconds before, so the enemy's counterplay is to kill her inside the window or to wait at the spot she will return to.
Her biggest survival tool, the Time Belt, has no pattern to link, so the strength it gives (escaping a bad fight with her health restored) is not listed as a link.

units.name: Cryocopter

tier.basis: Built at the Airbase once the construction yard or Command Hub near it has Heightened Clearance, one tech step beyond the basics; its infobox gives tier 2.

cost_band.basis: Its infobox price, which StrategyWiki repeats, is about one and a half times a main battle tank's: our high band.

mobility.notes: Its flying speed is three times the Conscript's walking pace. Among aircraft it keeps pace with the Soviet Twinblade helicopter, is quicker than the Imperial Chopper-VX, and is slower than the Allied jets, the Vindicator bomber and the Apollo fighter. As a helicopter it is a low flier here; in the source, as for every Red Alert 3 aircraft, only weapons that can attack air units reach it.

body.notes: A helicopter on a British airframe; the manual calls it a light helicopter. No source gives its dimensions (see uncertain).

armour.notes: Step 4 of the armour-class order decided: its armour set, a standard aircraft set that takes full damage from autocannon, flak and rocket fire and a little less from explosives, is not a plain armour word, and helicopters are light. The profile praises its fuselage as unusually sturdy for a helicopter, but patch 1.11 cut its health by about an eighth (Uprising keeps the older, higher value). The Advanced Aeronautics protocol gives every Allied aircraft a quarter more health.

sensors.notes: Its shroud-clearing figure equals the Conscript's, so medium; its plain vision figure is half as large again as the Conscript's. The Advanced Aeronautics protocol widens every Allied aircraft's shroud clearing by a quarter.

armament.name: Custom cryobeam
armament.summary: Does no damage at all. Held on a ground or sea target, the beam slows it more and more and then locks it in ice: a frozen unit cannot move, fire or use abilities, and a frozen building stops working. Frozen targets turn brittle, so almost any hit, even small-arms fire, shatters them; tesla, spectrum and radiation weapons are the exceptions and get no bonus. Several beams on one target freeze it faster, infantry freeze almost at once, and big targets take longer because the freeze is measured against the target's health. If nobody follows up, the ice thaws on its own. Reaches as far as the Conscript's rifle and cannot target aircraft. The High Technology protocol makes the beam stronger.

crew.notes: One player flies it and works both beams. In the fiction a pilot carries military scientists who run the equipment (background text and voice lines); that changes nothing here.

abilities.name: S.H.R.I.N.K. Beam
abilities.summary: A targeted ability on the special-ability key, fired at a vehicle or ship from about twice the cryobeam's reach; infantry are not affected. For a while the target is shrunk: it moves and fires faster, but deals only a quarter of its normal damage, reaches half as far, sees much less, takes double damage from everything, loses its own crushing and can be run over by any vehicle that crushes. Many shells and rockets also tend to miss a shrunken target, and a shrunken transport cannot take on infantry. It needs a cooldown between uses (no figure found); the High Technology protocol shortens it and makes the shrink last a few seconds longer.

strengths.why: Freezes any surface target solid, from infantry to the heaviest tanks, warships and factories; a frozen target is helpless and breaks under almost any hit.
As quick as any helicopter in the game, so it reaches a threat anywhere on the map fast.

weaknesses.why: Neither beam does real damage, so it kills nothing alone and, with no offensive weapon, never ranks up, not even through a Veteran Academy.
Freeze and shrink both wear off if nobody follows up, and tesla, spectrum and radiation weapons get no bonus against frozen targets.
Its beam reaches only surface targets, so it cannot fight back against aircraft.
A light airframe whose health patch 1.11 cut; StrategyWiki calls it vulnerable to enemy aircraft.

countered_by.why: It cannot target fliers at all, and StrategyWiki calls it vulnerable to enemy aircraft.

counters.why: Its main job is to stop the biggest threats, such as Apocalypse tanks and Dreadnought battleships, by freezing them until teammates break them.
Freezes artillery before it can shell base defences.
Infantry freeze almost at once, which makes it a good answer to a fast commando loose in a crowded base.
Given time it freezes a whole war factory, shutting the building down and leaving it brittle.

combos.why: Frozen targets are brittle enough that even small-arms fire breaks them, so cheap rifle infantry can finish what it freezes; the profile adds that one shotgun blast may wreck a frozen building.
Any vehicle that crushes can run over a target it has shrunk.
The same reason: StrategyWiki's Allied strategies page notes that shrunk enemies become easy prey for Guardian tanks to crush.

units.memorable: A helicopter with no gun at all: it freezes the enemy's biggest war machines solid for teammates to smash, or shrinks them into quick, feeble toys that anything heavy can roll over.
units.as_player: A fast, light T2 helicopter that deals no damage of its own. Hold left mouse on a ground target to slow it and then lock it in ice for your team to shatter; Q fires the shrink ray at a vehicle or ship, leaving it faster but feeble, fragile and easy to run over. Keep away from anti-air: you can hurt nothing, least of all aircraft.

The infobox also lists it among the unit's guns with a reach of its own, but no source describes a toggle between the two beams.

No source gives the cooldown. The High technology page of the Command & Conquer Wiki says that protocol cuts the Cryocopter's ability cooldown to three quarters and lengthens the shrink, so a cooldown exists; the band is left out.

The step-by-step slowing, the freeze measured against the target's health, frozen units being unable to use abilities, and the tesla, spectrum and radiation exceptions come from the Cryo page of the Command & Conquer Wiki, with the exceptions also in the Cryocopter page's trivia.

The infobox gives only a ground attack line and the profile says surface targets, so no air layer is listed. Naval follows the rule for games with ships; the Cryocopter page names Dreadnought battleships as targets.

Roles step 2 was applied although the unit has a weapon: the profile says it has no weapons in the usual sense and cannot harm any target, so the cryobeam is read as a tool. Read strictly as an armed unit, step 1 gives nothing (Special Weapons Support names support, whose requires it fails), steps 3 and 4 give nothing, and step 5 would make it a raider, since it is very fast and light.

No source gives its size. Medium is coded because the manual calls it a light helicopter, the size list's medium example for helicopters; large would follow if it were judged an attack or transport helicopter.
The comparisons with other aircraft rest on the airspeed figures in the Twinblade, Striker-VX, Vindicator and Apollo fighter infoboxes on the Command & Conquer Wiki.

Rests on the Allied Strategies page of StrategyWiki (https://strategywiki.org/wiki/Command_%26_Conquer:_Red_Alert_3/Allied_Strategies), which names the Guardian tank as the crusher for shrunk enemies, and on the Guardian tank page of the Command & Conquer Wiki, whose infobox gives it a crush level above the one a shrunk target keeps.
The health cut is from the patch 1.11 notes on the Cryocopter page; Uprising, which runs older unit data, keeps the higher value.

Left empty. Roles.secondary step 4 would offer raider for a very fast unit with light armour, but raider's description (hit and run, picking off isolated targets) needs damage, and the profile says it can do no harm to anything by itself, so raider is not a candidate. Scout fails the raider or scout tie-break: speed alone makes a scout only when official text calls the unit one.

fit_notes.note: No registered pattern covers shrinking an enemy vehicle for a time: it becomes faster and fires faster but hits much softer, reaches and sees less, takes double damage and can be crushed. mark-target only makes a target take more damage and disable-machine stops it, while this trades the target's speed up for a loss of power and toughness.

No weapon trait names a full freeze. Slow covers the build-up; root and silence together stand for the frozen state (no moving, firing or abilities), as the EMP tie-break codes a target that can do neither. The cryo family and the freeze-and-shatter pattern carry the brittle state that follows.

The strength the shrink ray gives (a vehicle made weak, fragile and crushable, from about twice the cryobeam's reach) has no pattern or other link that names it, so it is left out of strengths and described in the ability's summary.
